conclusions: For every finite-gauge X, its real-valued gauge norm is nonnegative.
For every finite-gauge X, its norm equals zero if and only if X is the zero almost-everywhere equivalence class.
For every finite-gauge X and Y, the norm of X+Y is at most the norm of X plus the norm of Y.
For every c ∈ ℝ and finite-gauge X, the norm of cX equals |c| times the norm of X.
mathematical_definitions: For a representative X and scale t, the modular is the ENNReal integral of ψ(|X|/t).
A scale is admissible when it is nonzero, finite, and the modular is at most one.
The extended gauge is the ENNReal infimum of admissible scales.
For an almost-everywhere equivalence class, the gauge is computed from a representative.
The finite-gauge space is the submodule of classes whose extended gauge is below infinity.
The real norm is the toReal value of the finite extended gauge.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every measurable space, probability measure, and Orlicz function, the Luxemburg gauge is a genuine real norm on the submodule of almost-everywhere real-valued function classes having finite gauge: it is nonnegative and definite, satisfies the triangle inequality, and is absolutely homogeneous.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The four laws are asserted only on the finite-gauge subtype.
Admissible scales explicitly exclude both zero and infinity.
If the admissible-scale set is empty, its ENNReal infimum may be infinity; such a class is excluded.
ENNReal.toReal does not represent infinity, but subtype membership ensures every converted gauge is finite.
ENNReal.ofReal truncates negative values; ψ's nonnegativity on the nonnegative arguments used here makes that truncation inactive.
The target uses almost-everywhere equivalence classes and a representative inside the modular.
No non-atomicity, extra integrability, or strict positivity of ψ away from zero is assumed.
The conjunction states four norm laws but does not assert completeness or a Banach-space structure.
ambiguities: The packet exposes IsProbabilityMeasure only through its opaque proposition-valued declaration, so its usual meaning relies on the conventional interface.
The one-level body of MeasureTheory.lintegral is opaque, so the packet does not independently expose every internal edge-case convention.
